BiblicalUsage: The word gongýzō carries the sense of murmur. In Matthew 20:11, the text says "they murmured against the goodman of the house." In Luke 5:30, the text says "But their scribes and Pharisees murmured against his disciples."
TheologicalSignificance: I take gongýzō to mean that sin is not a mistake; it is rebellion, and it needs a Saviour, not an excuse. That is why I keep this word in mind when I read those passages — it carries more than its size suggests.
RelatedEvents: The Feeding of the Five Thousand; The Calling of Matthew; The Parable of the Workers in the Vineyard
